subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a new normal-chat tool-error warning delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what should happen when a mutating tool fails but the assistant final reply sounds successful?
rationale: The remaining work adds public config surface and intentionally changes user-visible safety semantics for failed side effects, so source inspection cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Add an explicit delivery policy
options.body: Introduce an opt-in enum such as all/final/off while preserving the current default-visible safety behavior and covering config, docs, payload, progress, and channel tests.

options.title: Keep the boolean only
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported all-off operator knob and close or defer the success-aware enum request after documenting that contract more clearly.

options.title: Make it channel-specific
options.body: Put final-only/off behavior behind channel or deployment configuration for team-chat surfaces rather than adding another global message policy.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit delivery policy
recommendation.body: Introduce an opt-in enum such as all/final/off while preserving the current default-visible safety behavior and covering config, docs, payload, progress, and channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged warning-policy work and current blame make this the best available routing candidate for the safety/default contract decision.
